headline: Sr. Software Engineer | Design Systems, Accessibility & AI

experiences.titleOverride: Sr. Fullstack Engineer, Design Systems & Accessibility Lead

bullets.text: Built a two-way bridge between design and code with AI agents, writing skills that turn Figma designs into design-system code and code back into designs, so both stay in sync.
Work as engineering partner to product design, prototyping alongside designers and setting them up to prototype on their own with real design-system components.
Led the Figma Code Connect rollout, so engineers start from the real components, not just a mockup.

Made the design system compose cleanly with agentic tooling, enforcing conventions through type-safe utilities, strict wrappers, and GritQL, Biome, and ESLint rules that engineers and AI agents both follow.
Scaled AI-assisted development past personal use, with shared skills and agentic reviews for the team.
Earned design system adoption with tooling that tracks usage across repositories, plus regular feedback from engineers and designers to prioritize next steps.
Authored an accessibility training curriculum now in active use across SchoolAI, and have delivered two company-wide hands-on workshops so far.
Drove a company-critical accessibility initiative across 6 teams, closing 480 WCAG 2.1 issues and delivering SchoolAI's first VPAT, which unlocked major higher-ed and statewide deals.
Cut accessibility violations in new pull requests 80% over six months with AI review agents, as engineers internalized the patterns.
Built a real-time AI analysis layer over 17k+ daily student chats that gives teachers insights, sentiment, progress scoring, and alerts for concerning content.
Built React and TypeScript components for Lucid's design system, so teams didn't rebuild common UI.
Led Lucid's microinteraction initiative technically, selecting GSAP and building reusable tooling so teams could add polished motion without custom code.
Led a team of engineers, mentoring through regular 1:1s, targeted feedback, and code review.
Rebuilt canyonsdistrict.org from scratch, cutting average page load times 20%.
Architected a permissions allocation system with site-wide activity auditing and improved LDAP authentication, strengthening security and operational visibility.

body: The best design systems I've worked on share a quality that's hard to perfect. They make the right choice the easiest choice. Engineers build accessible, consistent interfaces not because they read the documentation, but because the components they reach for already do those things. Today that includes designers prototyping in code and the agents writing alongside them.

That's the work I've been doing on SchoolAI's design-system team. The biggest gap was between design and code, so I built skills that let AI agents turn Figma designs into design-system code and code back into designs, and a workflow that generates Figma components straight from production code. Now designers and engineers are always talking about the same implementation. I worked with our designers on tooling for our prototyping platform so their explorations start from real components, and our conventions are enforced in the tooling engineers and agents both run into. We track adoption across repositories, so when teams drift, we fix the system instead of the symptom.

I've spent some time looking through Thumbprint, and it's clear it was built around the same idea. Layering tokens, atomic utilities, and components lets teams step down a level instead of building something bespoke, which keeps the right thing easy and the wrong thing a little annoying. Helping designers and engineers move from idea to shipped product on that foundation is exactly the work I want to be doing.
I'd love to help engineer that pit of success for everyone building at Thumbtack, people and agents alike.
coverLetter.signoff: Thank you for your time & consideration,
